headline: This 2018 law sets many new research, technology-transfer, reporting, and program rules for the Department of Energy and its national laboratories.
what_it_does: The law lets some DOE national laboratories use technology-transfer funds for early-stage demonstrations and requires DOE to keep a searchable public database of its unclassified research contracts and grants. It bars laboratory contractors from charging general overhead costs to laboratory-directed research, with an exception for certain national security labs, and it creates or renames several research programs, including solar fuels, electricity storage, exascale computing, and a Facility for Rare Isotope Beams. It also makes Energy Innovation Hubs run by nonprofit consortia, keeps some commercial data from ARPA-E awardees out of Freedom of Information Act disclosure, and waives cost-sharing for universities and nonprofits for two years.

who_it_affects.how: They may not charge general and administrative overhead costs to laboratory-directed research, and they must meet new certification rules on competing with industry and avoiding conflicts of interest.
They are exempt from cost-sharing requirements for DOE research and development for two years.

who_it_affects.group: Private companies and entrepreneurs working with DOE
who_it_affects.how: They can make agreements with national laboratories under the expanded technology-transfer pilot program, and their commercial and financial information submitted to ARPA-E is protected from public release.

who_it_affects.group: Consortia applying to run Energy Innovation Hubs
who_it_affects.how: They must be made up of at least two qualifying entities, sign a binding partnership agreement, and operate as nonprofits.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers seeking DOE funding or access to exascale computers
who_it_affects.how: They may get competitively reviewed access to new exascale systems and can search a public database of DOE project awards.

when_it_takes_effect: Most provisions took effect when the law was enacted on September 28, 2018, though some reports and programs have their own deadlines and some pilot authority ran only through FY2019.
